3 2.
is filed by the Insurance Company, challenging the judgment and award dated NC: 2023:KHC-D:8840 19.12.2015, passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.996/2014, seeking reduction of quantum of compensation.
Whereas, MFA CROB No.100159/2016 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
4.
Brief facts of the case are that, on 07.03.2014 at about 6.45 p.m. the claimant was travelling on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-35/X-5222 at Sandur in front of S.L.R.Factory.

At that time,
driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA-34/2043 drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the claimant who fell down and sustained injuries.
5. In the present case, from the evidence placed on record, it is proved that claimant has suffered the following injuries.
i) Lacerated wound 1x1 Cms. Right upper eye lid.
ii) Abrasion right knee.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8840 iii) Lacerated wound 1x1 Cms.
Right knee.
iv) Contusion of the left foot.

6. The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as follows:
 Sl. Heads.

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Pain and suffering.
30,000  2. Loss of amenities and happiness.
Medical and incidental charges.

5,000  4. Loss of earnings during treatment 10,000  period.
 5. Loss of future earnings due to 1,26,000  disability.

The quantum of compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head pain and suffering, Rs.25000/-,
under the head loss of amenities and Rs.5,000/- under the head incidental charges, awarded by the tribunal are found to be correct.
Hence, they are kept intact.
But the tribunal has awarded combined compensation under head medical and incidental expenses.
Therefore, Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards medical expenses.

Sri.Shirivallappa @ Shiramalappa vs Sri.S Nageraj S/O Vallappa on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46891259/
4 NC: 2023:KHC-D:8840 8.
The claimant has produced the Adhar Card, which shows the date of birth as 12.07.1956.
The accident occurred on 07.03.2014.
Therefore as on the date of accident, the age of the claimant is proved to be 58 years.
But the tribunal has committed error in taking the age as 45 years.
Further, as the accident was of the year 2014, notional income would be taken as Rs.7,500/- per month as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The tribunal has held 15% functional disability, which is on higher side.
The claimant is an agriculturist.

Taking into consideration the nature of injuries suffered and disability occurred and avocation of the claimant is concerned as he is an agriculturist, 12% of functional disability is to be taken into consideration.
The claimant was aged 58 years.
Therefore, appropriate applicable multiplier is 9.

Hence loss of future income due to disability is hereby reassessed and quantified as Rs.97,200/- (Rs.7,500 x 12% x 12 x 9).
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8840 9.
Further, a compensation of Rs.22,500/- (Rs.7,500 x 3) is awarded under the head loss of earning during laid up period and treatment period for three months.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads. Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards injuries, pain and 30,000  suffering.
 2. Towards medical expenses.
5,000  3. Towards loss of amenities.

25,000  4. Towards loss of income during 22,500  laid up period and medical  treatment period.
 5. Towards incidental charges like 5,000  attendant charges, food,
 nourishment, etc.,.
 6. Towards loss of future earning 97,200  capacity.
 Total: 1,84,700  10.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,84,700/- as against Rs.1,96,000/- awarded by the tribunal i.e., reduced by Rs.11,300/-.
The claimant is entitled for interest on the compensation at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit NC:
2023:KHC-D:8840 the amount of compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
11.

Accordingly, I pass the following:

5 ORDER
i) The appeal filed by the insurance company in MFA No.101054/2016 is allowed in part.
ii) The cross objection filed by the claimant in MFA CROB No.100159/2016 is dismissed.

iii) The judgment and award dated 19.12.2015, passed by the III Addl. MACT, Ballari,
in MVC No.996/2014, stands modified.
iv) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,84,700/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8840 v) The insurance company shall deposit the compensation along with interest within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
vi) The remaining observations and findings made by the Tribunal in the aforesaid impugned judgment and award are kept in tact.
vii) No order as to costs.
viii) Draw award accordingly.
